2025-04-10: Inflation was cooler than expected, but tariff news dominated markets that day. A good example of other news swamping a data release.
2025-01-15: The headline number matched, but the 'core' measure (which leaves out food and energy) came in softer than expected, so stocks rallied and yields fell. The headline doesn't always tell the whole story.
2025-01-30: The Fed had held interest rates the day before, so traders were still digesting that.
2025-02-14: The day before, Trump announced plans for new “reciprocal” tariffs, so trade policy was on traders' minds.
2025-05-13: Markets were still reacting to the US-China tariff truce announced the day before, when the S&P 500 jumped more than 3%. The dollar gave back some of that rally.
2025-07-30: The Fed held interest rates that afternoon, with two members voting for a cut, and Powell gave no hint of a September cut. Yields and the dollar rose. The strong GDP number was also helped by a drop in imports.
2025-09-16: The Fed was due to decide the next day and a rate cut was widely expected, so the dollar was already sliding. The Swiss franc hit its strongest level against it in over a decade.
2025-12-16: This was a delayed jobs report covering two months. Unemployment rose to 4.6%, which first lifted bets on a Fed cut, but the move faded as stocks sold off and the dollar gained.
2025-12-18: This CPI looked unusually weak but was hard to trust: it was the first big report after the government shutdown disrupted data collection. Traders partly shrugged it off and stocks rose on tech earnings.
2026-01-14: Iran dominated: a report that Trump had decided on a military strike pushed gold to a record high and made stocks swing. The retail sales number was a sideshow.
2026-02-13: Inflation was softer, but markets were also jittery about AI-related volatility and bonds rallied as investors looked for safety.
2026-02-20: The Supreme Court struck down Trump's tariffs that day and he answered with a new 10% global tariff. That dominated trading far more than the weak GDP number.
2026-03-06: Oil jumped more than 10% on Middle East conflict and fears for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. That hit stocks harder than the weak jobs number.
2026-03-11: Inflation matched forecasts, but oil jumped about 5% on the US-Israel conflict with Iran, and a weak 10-year Treasury auction pushed yields higher.
2026-04-01: Hopes that the US-Iran conflict was nearing an end lifted stocks ahead of an address by Trump, with oil just under $100 a barrel.
2026-04-30: The Fed had held rates the day before with a hawkish tilt. On the day, the yen surged after Japan was reported to have intervened, and an AI-led rally took the S&P 500 to a record high.
2026-06-05: The jobs report was strong, but a tech-led selloff (the Nasdaq's worst day since April 2025, on worries about heavy AI-related share issuance), stalled US-Iran talks and a stronger dollar all hit markets, gold included.
2026-06-10: Inflation matched forecasts, but Trump threatened to strike Iran “very hard” and tech sold off ahead of the SpaceX IPO. It was an ugly risk-off day and gold broke lower.
2026-06-17: The Fed held rates, but Chair Warsh sounded hawkish on inflation. The dollar jumped, 2-year yields rose about 17 basis points and stocks fell 1.4%. That, not retail sales, drove the day.
2026-07-14: Fed Chair Warsh gave testimony to Congress (hawkish on inflation, no signal on rates), and Trump dropped a proposed fee on Strait of Hormuz shipping. The dollar and yields fell while stocks rose.
2026-07-30: The day after a Fed meeting, USD/JPY dropped sharply on speculation of Japanese intervention. A big tech-led rally lifted stocks while yields rose, despite the weak GDP.
2026-08-05: Gold surged with no clear trigger. Weaker ADP and ISM data, peace hopes and a weaker dollar may have helped.
2026-08-07: Payrolls fell, and markets decided a September Fed hike was now less likely than not. Gold rallied, and comments from Japan's finance minister moved USD/JPY too.
2026-09-16: The Fed raised interest rates for the first time in three years, in a unanimous vote, and Warsh sounded ready to hike again. Stocks fell about 1% and the dollar rose. Retail sales were secondary.
2026-10-02: Jobs were soft, but a tech-led rally took the Nasdaq 100 to a record close, and oil swung on news of emergency stockpile releases.
